prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE polished game prop design illustration for a 2D top-down dark-fantasy card game: a compact four-socket ARTIFACT CASKET docked into the PLAYER-SIDE WOODEN RAIL OF A BURGUNDY GAMING TABLE. This is a standalone close-up design study for review, NOT a whole game screen.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2, almost perfectly orthographic overhead, tactile hand-painted 2D illustration, fine ink contours and painted contact shadows, no photographic render and no isometric perspective. The complete casket occupies the central 75% of width, fully visible with breathing room. The upper quarter of the illustration shows a narrow adjacent dark wine-red felt playing surface; below it a substantial black-brown wooden table rail. The long shallow portable casket nests flush into this near-side rail, its raised rim and a thin shadow clearly separating it from the felt. No upright lid. Two small antique brass fastening clips visibly dock the casket to the rail.
Palette: dark burgundy #4a1724, antique gold #ac8c4e, black-brown walnut #261a15, restrained aged ivory. Material detail: gently worn black walnut grain, dark leather-lined recesses, tiny brass rivets, modest incised ornament and gently aged corners. Warm light from upper left. Rich but readable midtones, not crushed blacks, no excessive flourishes.
The casket has EXACTLY FOUR evenly spaced independent shallow round/oval sockets in ONE horizontal row, distinctly separated by wooden dividers. Left socket: an ornate palm-sized shield-shaped pendant with a deep burgundy enamel face, antique gold framework and a small ivory diamond in the center. Second socket: a narrow elongated dark red crystal suspended inside an antique-gold oval cage. Both relics lie FLAT, top-down, not standing. Each active socket has a thin segmented brass progress ring integrated into its base, with a few subtle amber-lit segments. Third and fourth sockets are visibly EMPTY dark leather-lined attachment nests with a restrained brass central mounting point, suggesting future equipment expansion. No extra relics.
Along the TOP edge of each socket, facing the felt, is a small card-width brass-edged delivery slit/lip. Show only ONE ornate ivory shield card half emerged from the FIRST delivery lip onto the burgundy felt: a captured completion instant. It has a fine antique-gold border and shield motif, no gameplay numbers or text. A restrained warm highlight connects the first relic to that slit through its own socket; no pipelines or global connecting wires. No permanent card storage tray and no deck stack. The card should be physically sized to fit the first outlet and clearly smaller than the width of one socket.
Minimal design annotations only, thin antique-gold leader lines outside the object and four accurately rendered Chinese labels: “独立法器匣” near lower left pointing to the outer rim; “成牌出口” in the upper left margin pointing to the first outlet; “批次刻度” near lower center pointing to the second socket progress ring; “扩展槽位” near lower right pointing between the two empty sockets. Small elegant readable lettering. No large title, no paragraph, no legend, no arrows traversing the object.
Avoid: game dashboard, web panels, HUD, buttons, hands, people, roulette, poker suits, betting amounts, candles, bottles, gears, factory machinery, sci-fi circuitry, blue neon, oversized lid, full table assembly, excessive text, watermark. The image should communicate a personal magical tool casket feeding cards into a nearby gaming surface, with visually distinct production and play areas.
